title: Logarithmic quality charts hide valid zero-defect results
reasoning: Lint and rubric aggregators accept zero as a valid metric, but both charts use logarithmic x axes, which cannot display zero. Runs with no lint errors or rubric flags disappear from the comparison. If annotated, a zero-valued point additionally receives annotation coordinate zero on the log axis, placing its label at data value 1 despite its marker being unrenderable.
reproduction: Render lint_vs_solve or rubric_vs_solve for a run whose corresponding mean ratio is zero and whose solve percentage is finite. Its marker cannot appear on the logarithmic axis.
recommendation: Use a zero-capable axis representation for quality metrics and keep annotation coordinates consistent with that representation.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The supplied scatter tests check missing time and catalog names, without rendering quality metrics or testing zero values.
suggestedRegressionTest: Cover zero and positive quality metrics together, verifying that all valid runs have representable marker and annotation coordinates in both single and multi-chart rendering.
minimumFixScope: Quality scatter axis configuration and associated annotation handling.

history.reasoning: The original evidence paths and lines still exist.
